text.p: International tie retailer Tie Rack Plc said on Thursday that recent trading has been satisfactory, but noted that the strength of sterling was continuing to pressure its overseas earnings.

With over 400 shops in 28 countries around the world the strength of the pound had an adverse impact on sales and profits of Tie Rack's overseas earners during its last quarter but it still managed to lift year profits 11 percent.

"Overall it could have a half to one percent effect on our overall growth margin (if sterling maintains current levels). But we still expect profitable growth in the year," chief executive Nigel McGinley told Reuters in an interview.
Earlier the group announced that pretax profits for the year to February 2, 1997, had risen 11 percent to 8.79 million stg. It raised its total dividend to 3.35p from 2.75p.
The company described trading in the first two months of the current year as "generally satisfactory".

McGinley said the company, with nearly 60 percent of its shops now overseas, was a little cautious on Europe given the depressed economic conditions in many European countries at present, but said that Europe would remain its main area of development for shop openings.
The company, however, is taking a cautious view of expansion in the UK given the current trend to higher rentals in the property market.
It remained confident that it would continue to make good progress in the U.S. and Far East.
It has already opened 12 shops this year and expects shop numbers to grow by around 10 percent this year with growth predominantly overseas.
It recently branched out into Eastern Europe for the first time when it opened in the Czech Republic.
